title: The Person of Christ
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The person of Christ means that Jesus Christ is one person with two natures: truly God and truly man. He is the eternal Son of God who took on human flesh, lived without sin, revealed the Father, died for sinners, rose from the dead, and reigns as Lord.
summary: The person of Christ means that Jesus Christ is one person with two natures: truly God and truly man. He is the eternal Son of God who took on human flesh, lived without sin, revealed the Father, died for sinners, rose from the dead, and reigns as Lord.
christFocus: Jesus is not merely a prophet, teacher, moral example, miracle worker, or religious leader. He is the Word made flesh, the image of the invisible God, the radiance of God’s glory, the only Mediator between God and man, and the risen Lord who gives life to all who believe in Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Jesus Christ is the eternal Son of God. He did not begin to exist at Bethlehem. Before creation, He was with God and was God. All things were made through Him, and in Him all things hold together. He shares the glory, authority, power, and nature of God, and He is worthy of worship, trust, obedience, and confession.

The same eternal Son truly became man. In the incarnation, the Word became flesh and lived among us. Jesus did not merely appear human; He entered real human life with a real body, real emotions, real weakness, real suffering, and real obedience. Yet He was without sin. Because He is truly man, He can represent us. Because He is truly God, He can save us.

The person of Christ is central to the Gospel. A merely human savior could not bear the full weight of sin and reconcile sinners to God. A savior who did not truly become man could not stand in our place. Jesus is fully God and fully man in one person, and this is why He alone is able to reveal God, redeem sinners, defeat death, intercede for His people, and bring them safely to glory.

All doctrine must be centered on Christ because all things find their meaning in Him. He is before all things, above all things, and the One through whom God is reconciling all things to Himself. The Christian faith does not rest on an idea, a system, a movement, or a moral code. It rests on the living person of Jesus Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
If people misunderstand Jesus, they will misunderstand salvation. A reduced Christ produces a reduced Gospel. If Jesus is treated only as a helper, example, prophet, healer, or inspiring teacher, people may admire Him without trusting Him as Lord and Savior. But Scripture presents Him as the eternal Son who became man to save sinners and reign over all.

This doctrine also gives deep comfort to the weak, ashamed, suffering, and rejected. The Savior is not distant from human pain. He entered it. He knows hunger, sorrow, temptation, rejection, grief, suffering, and death. Yet He is also mighty to save, able to forgive, able to restore, able to keep, and able to bring His people into the presence of God.

studySections.heading: Discipleship & Application
studySections.content: Come to Jesus as He truly is, not as culture, fear, religion, or personal preference imagines Him to be. Worship Him as God, trust Him as Savior, follow Him as Lord, depend on Him as Mediator, and draw near to Him as the One who understands your weakness. Let every part of your doctrine, ministry, recovery, suffering, obedience, worship, and hope be centered on the person of Christ.
